fixtures.rationale: The loop pushes each active pet into an array declared before the loop with no early exit, which a single filter call would express directly.
The loop pushes a transformed value for every element into an array declared above it, which a single map call would express directly.
The loop accumulates into a scalar declared before the loop with +=, which a single reduce call would express directly.
The loop assigns into an object declared before the loop keyed by each element, which Object.fromEntries or reduce would express directly.
The nested loop pushes every inner element into an array declared above both loops, which a single flatMap call would express directly.
The loop sets a flag declared before the loop once true and never exits early, which a single some call would express directly.
The loop's purpose is to register each route on the server as a side effect; it produces no collection or scalar result.
Each iteration awaits sending one email as a side effect and the order among reminders carries no meaning, so the loop performs effects rather than building a value.
The loop's only purpose is to log a message for each pet; it produces no value.
The loop writes each pet to an injected repository as a side effect and returns nothing, so it performs effects rather than building a value.
The loop deletes each file through an injected file system as a side effect and produces no value.
The loop compares each element against its neighbour by index and breaks on the first match, sequencing no single collection method expresses.
The while loop drains a queue whose length changes inside the body as new jobs are pushed, a shape no fixed-length collection method expresses.
The loop retries a request a bounded number of times, tracking an attempt counter and the last error across iterations, a sequencing no single collection method expresses.
The forEach body pushes a value derived from each element into an array declared before it and returns that array, which a single map call would express directly.
The filename matches the default test file pattern, so the rule produces no candidates at all regardless of its contents.
